note: Post-quantum and hybrid replacements FALCON recommends, with the sizes their standards define (bytes). Categories are NIST PQC security categories (1 ~ AES-128, 3 ~ AES-192, 5 ~ AES-256).

ML-KEM-768.summary: Module-lattice key encapsulation; the general-purpose default.

ML-KEM-1024.summary: Highest ML-KEM parameter set; required by CNSA 2.0.

X25519MLKEM768.summary: X25519 and ML-KEM-768 combined: secure if either holds. The default in current browsers, OpenSSL 3.5 and Go 1.24.

SecP384r1MLKEM1024.summary: P-384 and ML-KEM-1024 combined, for high-assurance and CNSA-aligned systems.

X-Wing.summary: A general-purpose hybrid KEM for applications and HPKE.

mlkem768x25519-sha256.summary: Hybrid ML-KEM key exchange for SSH.

IKEv2 + ML-KEM-768 (RFC 9370).summary: An additional ML-KEM exchange in IKEv2, keeping the classical one.

ML-DSA-44.summary: Smallest ML-DSA; for constrained, lower-assurance uses.

ML-DSA-87.summary: Highest ML-DSA parameter set; required by CNSA 2.0.

SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s.summary: Stateless hash-based signatures: conservative security, large and slow to sign. Suited to long-lived roots.

FN-DSA-512.summary: Compact lattice signatures for bandwidth-constrained protocols, once FIPS 206 is final.

LMS.summary: Stateful hash-based signatures for software and firmware signing (CNSA 2.0).

Composite ML-DSA-65 + ECDSA P-256.summary: One certificate carrying both signatures, for relying parties still on classical validation.

AES-256-GCM.summary: Authenticated encryption with a 256-bit key: keeps a 128-bit margin against Grover's algorithm.

CSPRNG.summary: The platform's cryptographic random generator (secrets, SecureRandom, crypto/rand).

java.name: Bouncy Castle 1.79+ or JDK 24+ (ML-KEM, ML-DSA)
java.summary: JDK 24 adds ML-KEM and ML-DSA; Bouncy Castle provides them for older JDKs.

go.name: Go 1.24+ (crypto/mlkem)
go.summary: crypto/mlkem and X25519MLKEM768 in crypto/tls by default.

python.name: cryptography with OpenSSL 3.5+
python.summary: ML-KEM and ML-DSA through pyca/cryptography on a recent OpenSSL.

javascript.name: @noble/post-quantum or Node.js on OpenSSL 3.5+
javascript.summary: Audited pure-JS ML-KEM and ML-DSA; hybrid TLS from the runtime.

rust.name: aws-lc-rs or RustCrypto ml-kem / ml-dsa
rust.summary: Production ML-KEM through aws-lc-rs; hybrid TLS in rustls.

c.name: OpenSSL 3.5+ or liboqs
c.summary: OpenSSL 3.5 ships ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA with hybrid TLS groups.

csharp.name: .NET 10 (MLKem, MLDsa)
csharp.summary: .NET 10 exposes ML-KEM and ML-DSA on supported platforms.

default.name: A library with FIPS 203/204 support
default.summary: Choose a maintained library that implements the NIST standards.
